summary.name: LLM Powered Autonomous Agents
summary.one_liner: A long-form survey blog post by Lilian Weng covering the design of LLM-powered autonomous agents, including planning, memory, tool use, and example systems.
keywords: ai agent planning memory tool use
use_cases: understanding how llm agents plan and decompose tasks
comparing agent memory and retrieval designs
reviewing agent case studies such as chemistry and simulation agents
background reading for building an llm agent
summary.what_it_does: This is a written overview, not a software product, of how an LLM can serve as the core controller of an autonomous agent. It covers planning techniques such as chain of thought, Tree of Thoughts, LLM+P with PDDL, and self-reflection methods including ReAct, Reflexion, Chain of Hindsight and Algorithm Distillation. It explains a memory model that maps short-term memory to in-context learning and long-term memory to external vector stores, and compares approximate nearest neighbor methods (LSH, ANNOY, HNSW, FAISS, ScaNN). It also describes tool-use systems (MRKL, TALM, Toolformer, HuggingGPT, API-Bank) and case studies such as ChemCrow, a generative agents simulation, and AutoGPT.
notable: Covers planning, memory, and tool use as the three core components of an LLM agent
Compares ANN indexes for fast maximum inner product search (LSH, ANNOY, HNSW, FAISS, ScaNN)
Includes case studies: ChemCrow, Generative Agents simulation, and scientific discovery agents
caveats: Describes research papers and early proof-of-concept demos, not a maintained software product
Notes that AutoGPT has reliability issues given the natural language interface
Mentions that LLM self-evaluation may fail in expert domains
